correctness.rationale: PASS: For degF<=1 the affine vector field is global; for odd positive-leading deg>=3 the Lyapunov energy E=(x^2+y^2)/2 obeys E_dot=-xF(x)<=C, excluding finite escape. All other nonaffine polynomials admit an orientation sigma with P(z)=-sigma F(sigma z)=a z^m+b z^{m-1}+O(z^{m-2}), a>0. In (z,v)=(sigma x,sigma y), z_dot=P(z)+v, v_dot=-z; on z>=R, -z<=v<=z the vector field points strictly inward on all three boundaries and z_dot>=(a/2)z^m, forcing finite-time blowup on an open sector. The exact orbit graph v_z=-z/(P+v) gives v=-(1/a)log z+C+o(1) in m=2 and v=v_inf+z^{2-m}/(a(m-2))(1+o(1)) in m>=3. The remaining-time integral gives 1/[a(m-1)] z^{1-m}-b/(a^2m) z^{-m}+o(z^{-m}), hence z=Z-b/(am)+o(1). In sextic P=z^6-z^3-alpha z, expansion of the integral yields z=Z+Z^-2/8+alpha Z^-4/10+O(Z^-5), x=-z and y_inf-y~Z^-4/4. These are all derived from inequalities/integrals, not finite sampling.
